- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (≤0.3) and forecast remains elevated, lower the forecast by 5–15% to reflect bearish sentiment.  
- After a forecast spike, apply a 3–5 day mean reversion correction downward if true outcome shows downward drift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, reduce forecasted mean by 2–5% to avoid lagged overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is high, apply a downward bias adjustment of 3–8% to align with pessimism.  
- Avoid forecasting above 85% of the 18-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.8) and recent price action confirms breakout.
